originalTitle: Inside India newsletter: Foreign insurers get the red-carpet treatment — and policy uncertainty
summary: Foreign insurers brace for another set of policy changes in India's insurance market.
content:
Hello, this is Priyanka Salve, writing to you from Singapore.

Welcome to the latest edition of " Inside India " — your one-stop destination for stories and developments from the world's fastest-growing large economy.

India's insurance sector has held a lot of promise for global companies, given low penetration rates and consequent reforms that have liberalized the industry. But recently proposed rules reintroducing commission caps could pour cold water on insurers' plans.

Global insurers eager for a bigger slice of the world's 10th-largest insurance market, after it allowed for 100% foreign ownership in the sector last December, are in for a rude surprise as the country's regulator plans to reverse one of its key reforms.

Last week, India's insurance regulator proposed the reintroduction of product-level commission caps, reversing its move in 2023 that allowed insurers flexibility over their commission structures.

While India's insurance market remains a long-term opportunity, experts warned that operational complexities ushered in by the frequent shifts in policy will make foreign investors pause their plans. If the proposals are agreed upon, insurers will have to comply by year ending March 2029.

The market was primed for cross-border deal activity after the foreign direct investment limit was raised to 100%, Debashish Banerjee, partner and insurance sector leader at Deloitte India, told CNBC.

But deals will be paused as managements and boards of foreign insurers will need to deliberate on the recent changes, he said, adding that more importantly, discussions will hinge on "what if six months down the road there will be another policy change?"

On Sept. 23, the regulator proposed new rules that seek to reinstate commission caps, tighten expense management limits and restructure remunerations to reward policy renewals instead of upfront sales volume.

State-owned firms such as the Life Insurance Corporation , SBI Life and New India Assurance are already operating within the proposed caps, as per local media reports. Other insurance companies, however, will need to cut total management expenses sharply, according to Indian credit rating agency Care Edge.

The proposals require private life insurers to cut total management expenses from 20% to 15% of gross direct premium income within two years and to 12.5% within five years, and general insurers to reduce it from 30% to 20% over five years, according to Care Ratings said.

"20 of 22 life insurers and 28 of 31 general insurers are above the proposed FY29 expense ceiling," the agency said.

Currently, the commission structures are very front-ended, with almost 35%-40% being paid out up-front to agents and the middlemen, which led to a lot of mis-selling of insurance products, Ramkumar Subramanian, partner for insurance at Grant Thornton Bharat, told CNBC.

The regulator wants to arrest this trend through the proposed changes, he said.

The market, however, was not thrilled with the announcement. A day after the new rules were proposed, India's largest online platform for insurance policies PB Fintech saw shares crash 36%, HDFC Life fell more than 6% and ICICI Life Insurance dropped 4%.

The new rules, if implemented, "substantially in the current form," could compress insurance distribution economics for banks and non-banking financial sector companies by 70%-90% in several high-margin categories, Citi said in a note.

The regulator has said the changes made in 2023 were "conceptually sound" but have "under-delivered on its objectives." It added that the removal of commission caps has increased commissions, especially among the private life and general insurers, as compared to state-backed sector insurers.

India's insurance market holds long-term promise because only 3.7% of people have an insurance policy, compared to the global average of 7.3%, Mohammad Hassan, head of APAC equities dividend forecasting at S&P Global Market Intelligence, told CNBC. As a result, foreign insurance companies have been keen to enter and expand their presence in the market, he said.

In May, U.K.-based Prudential acquired a 75% stake in India's Bharti Life Insurance, while a month later, Aviva acquired the remaining 25% stake .

According to local media reports, several other global insurance companies such as AXA, Chubb, Allianz, and Old Mutual have also been looking to invest in the country's insurance sector.

With hard caps set on distribution commissions, it could be a challenge for insurance companies to grow. Distribution channels play a crucial role in selling financial products such as insurance, which are seen as push products, but their commission has been an issue of contention with regulators across several countries.

Chubb and Axa did not respond to CNBC's request for comments.

The insurance sector is now grappling with the "blanket-capping" introduced by the regulator that does not consider different gestation periods and complexities of products, Subramanian said.

As per IRDAI's annual report for the year ended March 2025, India's insurance penetration remained at 3.7%, unchanged from a year ago, as its life insurance penetration declined from 2.8% to 2.7% and non-life penetration remained at 1%.

The regulator expects the latest regulations to help companies improve the reach of insurance products. But the Insurance Brokers Association of India has warned that "commission caps below the cost of servicing customers could make it difficult for insurers and intermediaries to reach customers in smaller towns and cities," as per local media reports.

If the regulator's latest move manages to make insurance products more appetizing to customers — even as it crimps distributors' margins — it could be a "net-positive" for foreign insurers. But for now, they exacerbate the operational challenges, especially for global insurers in a market where price points are already much lower than most mature markets, experts said.

chineseTitle: 印度内部时事通讯：外国保险公司受到红地毯待遇——以及政策的不确定性
chineseSummary: 外国保险公司正准备迎接印度保险市场的另一组政策变化。
chineseContent:
您好，我是 Priyanka Salve，从新加坡给您写信。

欢迎来到最新一期的《印度内部》——了解世界上增长最快的大型经济体的故事和发展的一站式目的地。

鉴于渗透率较低以及随之而来的行业自由化改革，印度保险业为跨国公司带来了很多希望。但最近提出的重新引入佣金上限的规则可能会给保险公司的计划泼冷水。

去年 12 月允许外资 100% 拥有该行业后，渴望在全球第十大保险市场中分得更大份额的全球保险公司，却因中国监管机构计划扭转其中一项关键改革而大吃一惊。

上周，印度保险监管机构提议重新引入产品级佣金上限，扭转了 2023 年允许保险公司灵活调整佣金结构的举措。

尽管印度保险市场仍然是一个长期机遇，但专家警告说，政策频繁变化带来的运营复杂性将使外国投资者暂停其计划。如果这些提议获得同意，保险公司必须在 2029 年 3 月结束的年度之前遵守。

德勤印度合伙人兼保险业负责人德巴什·巴纳吉 (Debashish Banerjee) 向 CNBC 表示，在外国直接投资限额提高到 100% 后，市场已为跨境交易活动做好了准备。

但他表示，由于外国保险公司的管理层和董事会需要审议最近的变化，交易将暂停，并补充说，更重要的是，讨论将取决于“如果六个月后再次出现政策变化怎么办？”

9 月 23 日，监管机构提出了新规则，旨在恢复佣金上限、收紧费用管理限制并重组薪酬以奖励保单续签而不是预售销量。

据当地媒体报道，人寿保险公司、SBI Life 和 New India Assurance 等国有企业已经在拟议的上限内运营。然而，印度信用评级机构 Care Edge 表示，其他保险公司将需要大幅削减总管理费用。

据 Care Ratings 称，这些提案要求私人人寿保险公司在两年内将总管理费用从直接保费总收入的 20% 削减至 15%，在五年内削减至 12.5%，普通保险公司则在五年内将管理费用从直接总保费收入的 30% 削减至 20%。

该机构表示：“22 家人寿保险公司中的 20 家和 31 家普通保险公司中的 28 家超出了拟议的 2029 财年费用上限。”

Grant Thornton Bharat 保险合伙人 Ramkumar Subramanian 告诉 CNBC，目前，佣金结构非常前端，几乎 35%-40% 预先支付给代理人和中间商，这导致了保险产品的大量不当销售。

他说，监管机构希望通过拟议的变革来遏制这一趋势。

然而，市场对这一消息并不感到兴奋。新规则提出一天后，印度最大的保险在线平台 PB Fintech 股价暴跌 36%，HDFC Life 下跌超过 6%，ICICI Life Insurance 下跌 4%。

花旗在一份报告中表示，如果新规则“基本上以目前的形式”实施，可能会将银行和非银行金融部门公司在几个高利润类别的保险分销经济性压缩70%-90%。

该监管机构表示，2023 年做出的改变“在概念上是合理的”，但“未能实现其目标”。它补充说，与国家支持的行业保险公司相比，取消佣金上限增加了佣金，特别是在私人人寿和一般保险公司中。

标准普尔全球市场情报公司亚太区股票股息预测主管穆罕默德·哈桑 (Mohammad Hassan) 向 CNBC 表示，印度保险市场拥有长期前景，因为只有 3.7% 的人拥有保险，而全球平均水平为 7.3%。他说，因此，外国保险公司一直热衷于进入并扩大在该市场的影响力。

5月，英国保诚集团收购了印度巴蒂人寿保险公司75%的股份，一个月后，英杰华集团收购了剩余25%的股份。

据当地媒体报道，AXA、Chubb、Allianz 和 Old Mutual 等其他几家全球保险公司也一直在寻求投资该国的保险业。

由于对分销佣金设定了硬性上限，保险公司的发展可能会面临挑战。分销渠道在保险等金融产品的销售中发挥着至关重要的作用，这些产品被视为推销产品，但其佣金一直是多个国家监管机构争论的问题。

Chubb 和 Axa 没有回应 CNBC 的置评请求。

萨勃拉曼尼亚表示，保险业目前正在努力应对监管机构引入的“一揽子上限”，该政策没有考虑不同的酝酿期和产品的复杂性。

根据 IRDAI 截至 2025 年 3 月的年度报告，印度的保险渗透率仍保持在 3.7%，与去年同期持平，其中寿险渗透率从 2.8% 下降至 2.7%，非寿险渗透率保持在 1%。

监管机构预计最新法规将帮助企业扩大保险产品的覆盖范围。但据当地媒体报道，印度保险经纪人协会警告称，“低于服务客户成本的佣金上限可能会使保险公司和中介机构难以接触到较小城镇的客户”。

如果监管机构的最新举措能够使保险产品更吸引客户——即使它压缩了分销商的利润——这对外国保险公司来说可能是一个“净利好”。但专家表示，就目前而言，它们加剧了运营挑战，特别是对于价格已经远低于大多数成熟市场的市场中的全球保险公司而言。

印度的病毒科克罗
